docs.text: HardFOC driver SFM Flow Meter Driver ¶ A header-only C++17 driver for Sensirion SF06-family gas mass flow meters such as the SFM4300. It identifies the part, starts a measurement for the right gas or O 2 mixture and reads flow, temperature and status with every word CRC-checked, on any MCU with I2C. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that writes and reads raw bytes on I2C and waits; it does the rest: command framing, CRC-8 checks, gas-table selection per part family, scaling to standard litres per minute and status decoding. Thermal mass flow meter for gas mixing SFM4300 Sensirion (SF06 family) Measures Gas mass flow, 0 to 20 slm (SFM4300-20) or 0 to 50 slm (SFM4300-50), and sensor temperature Gases O 2 , air, N 2 O, CO 2 and three O 2 mixtures (-20); O 2 , air and air/O 2 (-50) Interface I2C, 400 kHz typical, up to 1 MHz; address 0x2A to 0x2D (ADDR resistor); IRQn data-ready, active low Supply 3.0 V to 5.5 V, calibrated at 3.3 V; 4.2 mA measuring, 0.4 µA asleep (typical) Speed New flow value about every 0.5 ms (2 kHz); step response τ 63 under 5 ms Driver covers SFM4300, SFM3003, SFM3013, SFM3019, SFM3119 (SF06 command set) and SFM6000D (SFx6000) Datasheet · Sensirion reference driver What you get ¶ One object per sensor. sfm::Driver<YourI2c> covers every command of the SF06 set: start and stop, read, averaging, concentration update, scaling, sleep, product identifier and soft reset. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: identify the part, start a gas or a mixture, read, average, sleep and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Flow standing for sfm::Driver<MyI2c> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One sfm::Driver<I2cT> object per sensor, constructed with your port, the sensor's address and optionally the part family. Every command returns sfm::DriverResult<T> , never throws and never allocates. Task Calls Identify the part ReadProductIdentifier() , KnownVariant() , PartFamily() , AssumeVariant() Measure StartContinuous() , ReadMeasurement() , ReadFlowOnly() , Stop() Mixtures StartContinuous(gas, o2_permille) , UpdateConcentration() Configure ConfigureAveraging() , ReadScaleOffsetUnit() , SetAddress() Power EnterSleep() , ExitSleep() , SoftReset() State ActiveGas() , Measuring() , ActiveScaling() , Address() No bus access DecodeMeasurement() , EncodeWord() , DecodeWords() , sfm::Crc8() , sfm::StartCommandFor() , sfm::SupportsGas() SFx6000 only ReadTemperature() A DriverResult<T> has value and error . It converts to bool ( true when error is None ), and sfm::ToString(error) names the error for a log. Identify the part ¶ const auto id = flow . ReadProductIdentifier (); // idle mode only: before StartContinuous() or after Stop() if ( ! id ) { std :: printf ( "no reply: %s 
 " , sfm :: ToString ( id . error ). data ()); return false ; } std :: printf ( "product 0x%08lX, %s, %.0f slm full scale 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( id . value . product_id ), sfm :: ToString ( id . value . variant ). data (), static_cast < double > ( sfm :: FullScaleSlm ( id . value . variant ))); The sensor answers only in idle mode: before the first start, or after Stop() . The result sets the variant and the family the driver uses for every later start. Gases and part families explains why that matters. Start a measurement ¶ if ( ! flow . ConfigureAveraging ( 0 )) { // idle only: average-until-read (the default) return false ; } i2c . DelayMs ( 1 ); sfm :: Gas gas = sfm :: Gas :: CO2 ; if ( ! sfm :: SupportsGas ( flow . KnownVariant (), gas )) { gas = sfm :: Gas :: Air ; // SFM4300-50: O2, Air and Air/O2 only } if ( const auto r = flow . StartContinuous ( gas ); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "start failed: %s 
 " , sfm :: ToString ( r . error ). data ()); return false ; } const sfm :: Scaling & s = flow . ActiveScaling (); // read from the sensor for this gas std :: printf ( "scale %d, offset %d, unit 0x%04X 
 " , s . scale , s . offset , s . unit ); StartContinuous() checks the gas against the known variant, reads the scale factor, offset and unit for that gas (so the sensor must be idle), sends the start command and waits 12 ms for the first result. To change the gas, Stop() first. Read ¶ const auto m = flow . ReadMeasurement (); if ( m . error == sfm :: DriverError :: NoData ) { return ; // no new sample since the last read: skip this tick } if ( ! m ) { ++ errors ; // Crc: noise, missing pull-ups, a partial read return ; } const float slm = m . value . flow ; // (raw - offset) / scale const float t_c = m . value . temperature_c ; // sensor silicon temperature, SF06 parts only const bool fixed_n = m . value . status . fixed_n_averaging (); One read is one 9-byte transfer and three CRC checks. NoData is normal: the sensor NACKs a read while it has no new result. Call it at your control-loop rate, up to 2 kHz; Measurement and averaging explains what each read returns in each averaging mode. When you need only the flow, read one word instead of three: const auto f = flow . ReadFlowOnly (); // 3 bytes instead of 9: no temperature, no status if ( f ) { use_flow ( f . value ); } ReadFlowOnly() does not refresh the status or the temperature. Measure a mixture ¶ if ( ! flow . StartContinuous ( sfm :: Gas :: AirO2Mix , 400 )) { // 40.0 % O2 in air, in per mille (0 to 1000) return false ; } // Later, while measuring: no restart, no 12 ms gap. At most once per millisecond. if ( ! flow . UpdateConcentration ( 600 )) { // 60.0 % O2 return false ; } The argument is the O 2 volume fraction in per mille (0 to 1000); the driver refuses larger values with InvalidParameter (the sensor would stop measuring). UpdateConcentration() changes it without the 12 ms restart of a new start command. Send it at most once per millisecond, and do not read in between its two commands. Average on the sensor ¶ if ( ! flow . Stop ()) { // the sensor takes commands only in idle mode return false ; } i2c . DelayMs ( 1 ); // up to 0.5 ms until it is idle if ( ! flow . ConfigureAveraging ( 4 )) { // fixed N = 4: one value every 2 ms (500 Hz) return false ; } if ( ! flow . StartContinuous ( sfm :: Gas :: Air )) { return false ; } Averaging is configured in idle mode and holds until the next reset. 0 is average-until-read (the default), 1 to 128 is fixed-N. Sleep and reset ¶ if ( ! flow . Stop ()) { // continuous measurement to idle return false ; } i2c . DelayMs ( 1 ); if ( ! flow . EnterSleep ()) { // SF06 only, from idle: 0.4 uA typical return false ; } // ... later if ( ! flow . ExitSleep ()) { // a write header wakes it; polls until it ACKs return false ; } if ( const auto r = flow . SoftReset (); ! r ) { // general call 0x06, then 20 ms (SFx6000: 30 ms) return false ; // NotSupported: the port has no WriteGeneralCallImpl() } Sleep needs idle mode and is SF06-only. The sensor does not acknowledge the wake-up write; ExitSleep() polls the address in 5 ms steps for up to 20 ms. A soft reset is a general-call write that resets every device on the bus that supports it; after it, averaging is back to average-until-read and the sensor is idle. Read from an interrupt or DMA ¶ // frame: the 9 bytes your interrupt or DMA handler read after IRQn went low const auto m = Flow :: DecodeMeasurement ( flow . PartFamily (), flow . ActiveScaling (), frame ); if ( m ) { use_flow ( m . value . flow ); } DecodeMeasurement() is static and touches no bus: it checks the CRCs and scales the frame with the scaling of the active gas. Read the frame when IRQn falls; see Measurement and averaging . Handle errors ¶ const auto r = flow . StartContinuous ( sfm :: Gas :: N2O ); switch ( r . error ) { case sfm :: DriverError :: None : return true ; case sfm :: DriverError :: VariantUnknown : // N2O's start code means CO2 on SFx6000 parts ( void ) flow . ReadProductIdentifier (); // learn the family, then try again return flow . StartContinuous ( sfm :: Gas :: N2O ). ok (); case sfm :: DriverError :: UnsupportedGas : // this variant has no N2O table (SFM4300-50) return flow . StartContinuous ( sfm :: Gas :: Air ). ok (); default : // BusWrite, NoData, Crc, NotInitialized std :: printf ( "start failed: %s 
 " , sfm :: ToString ( r . error ). data ()); return false ; } Error Meaning What to do NoData The read was NACKed: no new sample yet, the sensor is idle, or nothing answered Skip the tick; if it persists, check the start and the address Crc A received word failed its CRC-8 Count it; persistent errors mean noise, weak pull-ups or a port that returns partial reads BusWrite A command write was NACKed or failed Address, wiring, or the sensor is measuring when the command needs idle NotInitialized The port's EnsureInitialized() returned false Bus set-up in your port UnsupportedGas The known variant has no table for this gas Use a gas from the table VariantUnknown The gas's start code depends on the family and the part is not known ReadProductIdentifier() or AssumeVariant() first InvalidParameter Averaging over 128, O 2 fraction over 1000 ‰ Fix the argument NotSupported The command does not exist on this family, or the port has no general-call write See Gases and part families BusRead and UnexpectedUnit are declared for logging compatibility; the current driver does not return them. SFx6000 temperature ¶ if ( flow . PartFamily () == sfm :: Family :: Sfx6000 ) { const auto t = flow . ReadTemperature (); // output-buffer pointer, while measuring if ( ! t ) { return false ; } use_flow ( t . value ); } On SFx6000 parts the second word of the measurement frame is reserved, so Measurement::temperature_valid is false ; ReadTemperature() moves the output-buffer pointer, reads one word and moves it back. On SF06 parts it returns NotSupported : the temperature is in every frame. Next: Configuration .

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the sensor. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one sfm::Driver object per sensor, whose public commands are listed from inc/sfm_driver.hpp. The core turns each call into 16-bit SF06 commands, checks the CRC-8 of every word it reads and converts raw counts with the scaling the sensor reported. The communication interface (sfm::I2cInterface in inc/sfm_i2c_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base: four methods are required, general call is optional. The platform port is the only code you write. Below it is the sensor. Drawn from: inc/sfm_driver.hpp Driver public commands ; inc/sfm_i2c_interface.hpp I2cInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where Depends on You change it when Hardware-agnostic core : sfm::Driver<I2cT> inc/sfm_driver.hpp , inc/sfm_types.hpp , inc/sfm_commands.hpp The interface's methods only Never, for a new board Communication interface : sfm::I2cInterface<Derived> inc/sfm_i2c_interface.hpp Four methods of your port, one optional Never Platform port : your class Your project Your SDK Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test fake. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the sensor ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as sfm::Driver participant P as Your port participant S as SFM4300 A->>D: StartContinuous(Gas::Air) D->>D: gas allowed for this variant? D->>P: Write(0x2A, 36 61 36 08 CRC) P->>S: scaling request for air D->>P: Read(0x2A, 9 bytes) S-->>P: scale, offset, unit + CRCs P-->>D: bytes, CRCs checked D->>P: Write(0x2A, 36 08) D->>P: DelayMs(12) D-->>A: DriverResult<void> ok A->>D: ReadMeasurement() D->>P: Read(0x2A, 9 bytes) P-->>D: flow, temperature, status D-->>A: Measurement in slm What the core keeps ¶ The driver object holds a handful of values between calls, and no buffers: State Set by Used for Address Constructor, SetAddress() Every transfer Part family ( Sf06 or Sfx6000 ) Constructor, ReadProductIdentifier() , AssumeVariant() Which start code means which gas; frame layout; which commands exist Variant ReadProductIdentifier() , AssumeVariant() Which gases are calibrated ( SupportsGas() ) Scaling of the active gas StartContinuous() Raw counts to slm in every read Active gas, measuring flag StartContinuous() , Stop() , SoftReset() ActiveGas() , Measuring() Why CRTP ¶ The interface is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The optional WriteGeneralCallImpl() is detected at compile time: a port without it still compiles, and SoftReset() returns NotSupported . The cost is that the driver type names the port: sfm::Driver<MyI2c> . Results instead of exceptions ¶ Every command returns sfm::DriverResult<T> : a value and an error ( sfm::DriverError ). It converts to bool , so if (!r) is the check. ToString(error) gives a stable name for logs. The API guide lists what each error means. docs.text: The interface is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The optional WriteGeneralCallImpl() is detected at compile time: a port without it still compiles, and SoftReset() returns NotSupported . The cost is that the driver type names the port: sfm::Driver<MyI2c> .

docs.text: I2C protocol ¶ The SF06 command set as the driver uses it: framing, every command, the frames the sensor returns, scaling and the status word. Source: SFM4300 datasheet , section 4. The constants are in inc/sfm_commands.hpp . Framing ¶ A command is 16 bits , MSB first, written without a register byte. A command with an argument adds a 16-bit argument and its CRC-8 : five bytes in all. A read returns 16-bit words, each followed by a CRC-8 . The host may stop after any word with a NACK and a STOP. The driver checks every CRC and returns DriverError::Crc on the first mismatch. The CRC-8 covers the two bytes before it: polynomial 0x31 (x⁸ + x⁵ + x⁴ + 1), initial value 0xFF, no reflection, no final XOR. Test vector: CRC(0xBEEF) = 0x92, checked at compile time by a static_assert . Commands ¶ Code Command (argument) Driver call, notes 0x3603 Start, O 2 StartContinuous(Gas::O2) 0x3608 Start, air StartContinuous(Gas::Air) 0x3615 Start, N 2 O StartContinuous(Gas::N2O) ; SFM4300-20 only 0x361E Start, CO 2 StartContinuous(Gas::CO2) ; SFM4300-20 only 0x3632 Start, air / O 2 (O 2 ‰) StartContinuous(Gas::AirO2Mix, o2) 0x3639 Start, N 2 O / O 2 (O 2 ‰) StartContinuous(Gas::N2OO2Mix, o2) ; SFM4300-20 only 0x3646 Start, CO 2 / O 2 (O 2 ‰) StartContinuous(Gas::CO2O2Mix, o2) ; SFM4300-20 only 0xE17D Transmit concentration (O 2 ‰) UpdateConcentration() ; while measuring 0xE000 Reset I2C address pointer UpdateConcentration() , after 0xE17D 0x3FF9 Stop continuous measurement Stop() ; idle after up to 0.5 ms 0x366A Configure averaging (N) ConfigureAveraging() ; idle only; 0 = average-until-read, 1 to 128 = fixed N 0x3661 Read scale factor, offset, unit (start code) ReadScaleOffsetUnit() ; idle only; three words back 0x3677 Enter sleep EnterSleep() ; idle only (address + W) Exit sleep ExitSleep() ; not acknowledged, poll until the address ACKs (typically 16 ms) 0xE102 Read product identifier ReadProductIdentifier() ; idle only; six words back 0x06 to 0x00 Soft reset (general call) SoftReset() ; about 16 ms, 20 ms maximum Codes 0x3624 and 0x362F are reserved on the SFM4300. While a continuous measurement runs, the sensor accepts only stop, soft reset and the two concentration commands: stop it before anything else. Frames the sensor returns ¶ After Words (each + CRC) Bytes A start command flow, temperature, status 9 (3 for flow only) 0x3661 scale factor, offset, unit 9 0xE102 product number (2 words), serial number (4 words) 18 Flow, temperature, scale factor and offset are signed 16-bit (two's complement); the unit and the status are unsigned. A read header while no new sample exists is NACKed ( DriverError::NoData ). Scaling ¶ The sensor reports raw counts. The physical value is (raw - offset) / scale , with the scale factor and offset of the gas table in use: Signal Scale factor Offset Unit Flow, SFM4300-20 (every gas and mixture) 2500 -28672 slm Flow, SFM4300-50 (O 2 , air, air/O 2 ) 1000 -28672 slm Temperature 200 0 °C The driver does not hard-code the flow scaling: StartContinuous() reads it from the sensor ( 0x3661 ) for the gas you start, and ReadMeasurement() applies it. The temperature scale (200 per °C) is a constant, sfm::kTemperatureScalePerC . The flow unit is 0x0148 on every SFM4300 table: standard litres per minute at 20 °C and 1013.25 mbar (bits 12:8 = 1 standard litre, bits 7:4 = 4 per minute, bits 3:0 = 8 prefix 10⁰). Status word ¶ The third word of each measurement frame. docs.text: A command is 16 bits , MSB first, written without a register byte. A command with an argument adds a 16-bit argument and its CRC-8 : five bytes in all. A read returns 16-bit words, each followed by a CRC-8 . The host may stop after any word with a NACK and a STOP. The driver checks every CRC and returns DriverError::Crc on the first mismatch. The CRC-8 covers the two bytes before it: polynomial 0x31 (x⁸ + x⁵ + x⁴ + 1), initial value 0xFF, no reflection, no final XOR. Test vector: CRC(0xBEEF) = 0x92, checked at compile time by a static_assert .

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++17 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++17 compiler: GCC 9+, Clang 10+ or the ESP-IDF toolchains. CMake 3.16 or newer, if you use the CMake target. An I2C controller that can do raw writes and reads to a 7-bit address (no register byte), and, for SoftReset() , a one-byte write to the general-call address 0x00. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every call is noexcept and returns sfm::DriverResult<T> . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-sfm-flow-meter-driver.git external/hf-sfm-flow-meter-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-sfm-flow-meter-driver Only inc/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-sfm-flow-meter-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::sfm ) hf::sfm (the hf_sfm target) is an INTERFACE library: it carries the include directories, including the generated sfm_version.h , and requires C++17 ( cxx_std_17 ). Option Default Effect HF_SFM_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF Adds -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic to targets that link hf::sfm HF_SFM_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests and the documentation snippets in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) Without add_subdirectory , include the build settings and use their include list: include ( external/hf-sfm-flow-meter-driver/cmake/hf_sfm_build_settings.cmake ) target_include_directories ( my_app PRIVATE ${ HF_SFM_PUBLIC_INCLUDE_DIRS } ) target_compile_features ( my_app PRIVATE cxx_std_17 ) ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_sfm/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_SFM_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. docs.text: Measurement and averaging ¶ What one read returns, how often to read, and how the sensor's averaging and IRQn line change that. The measurement loop ¶ After a start command the sensor measures continuously, about every 0.5 ms (2 kHz). Each read of the result buffer returns the latest value of three signals: flow, temperature and the status word. The flow is averaged on the sensor in one of two modes; the temperature updates at about 90 Hz. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle: power-up or soft reset Idle --> Measuring: start command (12 ms to first result) Measuring --> Measuring: read, update concentration Measuring --> Idle: Stop() (up to 0.5 ms) Idle --> Sleep: EnterSleep() Sleep --> Idle: ExitSleep() (typically 16 ms) Only idle mode accepts configuration commands: averaging, scaling, product identifier and sleep. While measuring, the sensor takes stop, soft reset and the concentration update, and nothing else. Average-until-read (default) ¶ ConfigureAveraging(0) , and the mode after power-up and after a reset. The sensor averages every sample since the previous read, so a read at any rate returns the mean over the whole interval: a fixed-rate poll is anti-aliased without a filter on the host. For the first 64 ms after a read the average is the arithmetic mean. If you wait longer, the sensor switches to exponential smoothing with α = 0.02 (status bit 11 set), which weights roughly the last 64 ms. Read at least every 64 ms to keep the plain mean. Fixed-N averaging ¶ ConfigureAveraging(N) with N from 1 to 128: each result is the mean of N samples, so a new result is ready every N × 0.5 ms. Reading earlier gets a NACK ( DriverError::NoData ). N = 1 turns averaging off. Status bit 10 is set in this mode. N New result every Rate 1 0.5 ms 2 kHz 4 2 ms 500 Hz 20 10 ms 100 Hz 128 64 ms about 16 Hz Configure averaging in idle mode, before StartContinuous() ; the setting holds until a reset or the next ConfigureAveraging() . The driver accepts 0 to 128 and returns InvalidParameter above. The IRQn line ¶ IRQn goes low when a new result is ready (at 2 kHz, or 2 kHz / N with fixed-N averaging) and returns high when the result is read. It is also low after power-up or a reset, until a start command. So a low IRQn after a start means "result ready", unless the sensor was reset, in which case the read is NACKed. Use it to read only when there is data: wait for the falling edge in a GPIO interrupt, read the 9-byte frame there (or start a DMA transfer) and decode it with Driver::DecodeMeasurement() , which needs no bus access. The API guide shows it. Leave IRQn unconnected if you poll. What "NoData" means ¶ A read header with no new result is NACKed by design. The driver reports it as DriverError::NoData : skip the tick and read again later. It is a fault only when it never stops, which means the sensor is idle (no start, or it was reset) or the address is wrong. Start-up ¶ Time after the start command State 0 to 12 ms No result; reads are NACKed. StartContinuous() waits these 12 ms 12 ms to 30 ms Results arrive but can be a few percent off while the heater warms up From 30 ms Results within the datasheet accuracy Changing the gas with a new start command costs the same 12 ms, and 70 ms until the reading settles. To change only the O 2 fraction of a mixture, use UpdateConcentration() : it does not interrupt the measurement. Next: Gases and part families .

docs.text: Gases and part families ¶ Which gas tables each part carries, why the driver needs to know the part before it starts some gases, and how the SF06 and SFx6000 families differ. Gas tables by variant ¶ A thermal flow sensor is calibrated per gas. Measuring CO 2 with the air table gives a reading that is plausible and wrong. The driver therefore refuses a gas the known variant is not calibrated for, with DriverError::UnsupportedGas . Variant Range Calibrated gases SFM4300-20-B, -O, -P 0 to 20 slm O 2 , air, N 2 O, CO 2 , air/O 2 , N 2 O/O 2 , CO 2 /O 2 SFM4300-50-B, -O, -P 0 to 50 slm O 2 , air, air/O 2 SFM6000D-50, -20, -5 50, 20, 5 slm (air, O 2 ) O 2 , air, N 2 O, CO 2 , Ar, air/O 2 Unknown O 2 , air The SFM4300 rows come from the SFM4300 datasheet (sections 2.1 and 4.5). sfm::SupportsGas() encodes the table; sfm::FullScaleSlm() gives the air / O 2 full scale of a known variant. Why the part has to be known ¶ The two families share the framing and most command codes, but two start codes mean different gases: Start code SF06 (SFM4300, SFM3xxx) SFx6000 (SFM6000D) 0x3603 O 2 O 2 0x3608 Air Air 0x3615 N 2 O CO 2 0x361E CO 2 N 2 O So until the driver knows the family, it starts only O 2 and air, the two codes that mean the same gas on both. Any other gas returns DriverError::VariantUnknown . Learn the part in one of two ways: ReadProductIdentifier() , in idle mode: it decodes the variant and sets the family. AssumeVariant() , when the identifier cannot be read (the sensor is already measuring) and the board fixes the part ( Configuration ). The constructor's family argument only sets the assumption used before either of those. Never pick a start code yourself: sfm::StartCommandFor(family, gas) returns the right one, and a static_assert in the header pins the CO 2 codes of both families. SF06 and SFx6000 compared ¶ SF06 SFx6000 Parts SFM4300, SFM3003, SFM3013, SFM3019, SFM3119 SFM6000D Measurement frame flow, temperature, status flow, reserved, status Temperature In every frame ReadTemperature() , through an output-buffer pointer Sample period 0.5 ms 1 ms Scaling read Three words Five words through pointer 0xE151 : adds full-scale flow and the SEMI gas ID Averaging, sleep Yes No: ConfigureAveraging() , EnterSleep() , ExitSleep() return NotSupported Soft-reset wait 20 ms 30 ms Default address 0x2A (SFM4300) 0x24 The SFx6000 values come from Sensirion's SFC6xxx / SFM6xxx I2C interface reference (v1.1), as implemented in inc/sfm_commands.hpp . The SFM6000D product identifiers are preliminary in that document; the driver decodes 0x060211xx , 0x060212xx and 0x060214xx . Other SF06 parts ¶ SFM3003, SFM3013, SFM3019 and SFM3119 speak the same command set at their own addresses ( sfm::addr ). The driver reads their scaling from the sensor, so readings are right, but it has no Variant for them and does not decode their product identifiers: their variant stays Unknown , which limits them to O 2 and air. Pass the part's address to the constructor (for example sfm::addr::kSfm3019 ). Next: API guide .

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the I2C interface. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls four methods, plus one optional, on a class you derive from sfm::I2cInterface<Self> (in inc/sfm_i2c_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one sfm::Driver object per sensor, whose public commands are listed from inc/sfm_driver.hpp. The core turns each call into 16-bit SF06 commands, checks the CRC-8 of every word it reads and converts raw counts with the scaling the sensor reported. The communication interface (sfm::I2cInterface in inc/sfm_i2c_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base: four methods are required, general call is optional. The platform port is the only code you write. Below it is the sensor. Drawn from: inc/sfm_driver.hpp Driver public commands ; inc/sfm_i2c_interface.hpp I2cInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract Write(addr7, data, len) yes START, address + W, len bytes, STOP. No register byte. len == 0 is an address-only probe. docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Read a gas flow from your MCU: wire four signals, write a small port class, call three driver functions. 1. Wire it ¶ The SFM4300 has a 6-pin JST NSH connector (1.0 mm pitch). MCU SFM4300 pin Notes I2C SDA 2 (SDA) Pull-up to the MCU's I/O voltage (2.2 kΩ to 4.7 kΩ is typical) I2C SCL 5 (SCL) Pull-up as SDA; 400 kHz is the typical clock, 1 MHz the maximum 3.3 V 4 (VDD) 3.0 V to 5.5 V; the sensor is calibrated at 3.3 V GND 3 (GND) Common ground (none) 1 (ADDR) Leave open or tie to GND for address 0x2A; never tie it to VDD GPIO in (optional) 6 (IRQn) Low when a sample is ready; leave it unconnected if unused The Hardware page has the other addresses, the electrical limits and the timing. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf::sfm CMake target (or add inc/ to your include path and build with C++17). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-sfm-flow-meter-driver.git external/hf-sfm-flow-meter-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code. It writes and reads raw bytes to a 7-bit address and waits. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public sfm :: I2cInterface < MyI2c > { public : // Raw write: START, address + W, the bytes, STOP. No register byte. len == 0 is an // address-only probe (ExitSleep() uses it). Return false on a NACK or bus error. bool Write ( uint8_t addr7 , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr7 , data , len ); } // Raw read: START, address + R, len bytes, STOP. Return false on a NACK: the sensor // NACKs its address while it has no new sample, and the driver reports NoData. bool Read ( uint8_t addr7 , uint8_t * out , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_read ( addr7 , out , len ); } // Blocking wait: start-up (12 ms), soft reset (20 or 30 ms), wake-up polling (5 ms steps). void DelayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_ms ( ms ); } // Bring the bus up on first use; every command checks it. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // Optional: one byte to the general-call address 0x00. Without it SoftReset() returns NotSupported. bool WriteGeneralCallImpl ( uint8_t byte ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( sfm :: addr :: kGeneralCall , & byte , 1 ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Read() must return false when the sensor NACKs its address: that is how the SFM4300 says "no new sample yet". Porting explains each method. 4. Read a flow ¶ main.cpp #include "sfm.hpp" int read_air_flow ( MyI2c & i2c , float & slm ) { sfm :: Driver < MyI2c > flow ( i2c , sfm :: addr :: kSfm4300Default ); // ADDR to GND: 0x2A const auto id = flow . ReadProductIdentifier (); // 1. identify (idle mode only) if ( ! id ) { return -1 ; // wiring, pull-ups or address } if ( ! flow . StartContinuous ( sfm :: Gas :: Air )) { // 2. read the scaling, start, wait 12 ms return -2 ; } const auto m = flow . ReadMeasurement (); // 3. flow, temperature, status if ( ! m ) { return m . error == sfm :: DriverError :: NoData ? 1 : -3 ; // NoData: no new sample yet } slm = m . value . flow ; // standard litres per minute return 0 ; } What each step does: ReadProductIdentifier() reads the 32-bit product number and serial number and decodes the variant (for example SFM4300-20-P). The sensor answers it only in idle mode, so call it before starting. StartContinuous() reads the scale factor, offset and unit for the gas, sends the start command and waits the 12 ms until the first result is ready. ReadMeasurement() reads one 9-byte frame (flow, temperature, status), checks three CRCs and converts the flow to standard litres per minute (slm, at 20 °C and 1013.25 mbar). Results are accurate after about 30 ms of measuring: discard the first readings. Poll at any rate up to 2 kHz; in the default averaging mode each read returns the mean of the samples since the previous read. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check ReadProductIdentifier() returns NoData or BusWrite Pull-ups, the address (ADDR strap), SDA and SCL swapped, the sensor powered It fails only after a start The sensor takes commands only in idle mode: call Stop() first ReadMeasurement() always returns NoData No start command was sent, or the poll is faster than the sample rate Occasional Crc errors Weak pull-ups or long wires; lower the clock to 100 kHz ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : gases and mixtures, averaging, sleep, errors. docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up an SF06 flow meter, their causes and the fix for each. Start with the error the call returned ( sfm::ToString(r.error) ): it separates bus problems ( BusWrite , NoData on every call) from data problems ( Crc ) and from configuration problems ( UnsupportedGas , VariantUnknown ). Nothing answers ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Every call returns BusWrite or NoData Wrong address Check the ADDR strap: open or GND is 0x2A ; scan the bus No pull-ups, or SDA and SCL swapped External pull-ups on both lines; check the connector pin order (SDA is pin 2, SCL pin 5) The sensor is still starting Wait 20 ms after power-up before the first call ADDR tied to VDD Not allowed: tie it to GND or leave it open NotInitialized The port's EnsureInitialized() failed Your bus set-up (for the ESP32 port: call Install() first) Reads fail ¶ Symptom Cause Fix NoData on every read No start command, Stop() was sent, or the sensor was reset (IRQn low after a start) Call StartContinuous() again NoData on some reads Polling faster than results arrive: 2 kHz, or 2 kHz / N with fixed-N averaging Expected: skip the tick, or read on the IRQn edge Crc now and then Noise, slow edges, weak pull-ups, long cable Stronger pull-ups, shorter wires, 100 kHz Crc on every read The port returns fewer bytes than asked, or reads with a register byte Fix the port ( Porting ) Commands are refused ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Identifier, averaging or a new start fails The sensor is measuring; it takes these only in idle mode Stop() , wait 0.5 ms, then the command UnsupportedGas The variant has no table for the gas (for example CO 2 on an SFM4300-50) Use a calibrated gas ( Gases and part families ) VariantUnknown The gas's start code depends on the family ReadProductIdentifier() in idle mode, or AssumeVariant() NotSupported from SoftReset() The port has no WriteGeneralCallImpl() Add it, or power-cycle the sensor NotSupported from averaging or sleep SFx6000 part These commands exist only on SF06 parts ExitSleep() returns BusWrite The port cannot send an address-only write ( len == 0 ) Support empty writes in Write() Do not bypass UnsupportedGas with AssumeVariant() : a thermal sensor read with the wrong gas table gives a plausible, systematically wrong flow. Readings look wrong ¶ Symptom Cause Fix The first readings are a few percent off Warm-up: accuracy is reached about 30 ms after the start Discard readings for 30 ms after each start A reading lags a step change Average-until-read smooths exponentially when you read less often than every 64 ms (status bit 11) Read at least every 64 ms, or use fixed-N averaging A constant offset The sensor is not horizontal, or the line pressure is outside 0.66 bar to 7 bar absolute Mount it horizontally with the connector up ( Hardware ) The temperature differs from the gas temperature The sensor reports its silicon temperature Expected; insulate the sensor if you need the gas temperature The status shows the wrong mixture GasFromStatusNibble() maps SF06 mixtures to 4 to 6; the datasheet uses 6 to 8 Use ActiveGas() ( I2C protocol )

docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The first readings are a few percent off Warm-up: accuracy is reached about 30 ms after the start Discard readings for 30 ms after each start A reading lags a step change Average-until-read smooths exponentially when you read less often than every 64 ms (status bit 11) Read at least every 64 ms, or use fixed-N averaging A constant offset The sensor is not horizontal, or the line pressure is outside 0.66 bar to 7 bar absolute Mount it horizontally with the connector up ( Hardware ) The temperature differs from the gas temperature The sensor reports its silicon temperature Expected; insulate the sensor if you need the gas temperature The status shows the wrong mixture GasFromStatusNibble() maps SF06 mixtures to 4 to 6; the datasheet uses 6 to 8 Use ActiveGas() ( I2C protocol )

Three layers, one of them yours ¶ Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one sfm::Driver object per sensor, whose public commands are listed from inc/sfm_driver.hpp. The core turns each call into 16-bit SF06 commands, checks the CRC-8 of every word it reads and converts raw counts with the scaling the sensor reported. The communication interface (sfm::I2cInterface in inc/sfm_i2c_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base: four methods are required, general call is optional. The platform port is the only code you write.
